contracts.commit_point: task.status = new_status.value assigned at task_service.py:121 and persisted by db.flush() at task_service.py:127 inside transition(), reached from complete() at task_service.py:253 with TaskStatus.COMPLETED.
contracts.declared_mechanism: task_service.complete() runs evaluate_completion (acceptance-criteria check, test-evidence check, pull-request-claim check, deployment-claim check, errors_or_warnings check), applies the evidence to the task, and on any blocking reason flushes a task.complete_blocked audit record with outcome DENIED and raises CompletionBlocked; only otherwise does it call transition(), which additionally enforces the ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS state machine (raising TransitionError on disallowed moves).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Marking a Task COMPLETED when evaluate_completion returns any blocking reason: a missing or False acceptance-criterion result, missing or non-passing unit tests for a software task, any failing recorded test result, pull_request_merged claimed without a pull_request_url, a deployment claimed without a provider-confirmed success status, or unresolved errors_or_warnings present — i.e., completion asserted from natural-language success claims without structural evidence.
pending_binding_information: Which agent tool, lifecycle hook, or route invokes task_service.complete() — required to establish agent mediation (direct_tool or agent_generated_input_to_guarded_effect).
Whether CompletionEvidence fields are validated as agent-generated inputs at any dispatch boundary; no such validation surface is shown in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: The task completion transition: task_service.complete() evaluating CompletionEvidence and, only on success, calling transition() to set TaskStatus.COMPLETED.
contracts.protected_resource: Task status/state records (status, completed_at, and the persisted evidence fields written by _apply_evidence).
contracts.protection_obligation: A Task may transition to COMPLETED only through task_service.complete(), which commits the transition only when deterministic, structurally supplied evidence passes evaluation: every acceptance criterion has a True recorded result, required test evidence is present and passing, pull-request-merge and deployment claims are provider-backed, and no unresolved errors_or_warnings remain; otherwise complete() records a DENIED audit event and raises CompletionBlocked instead of committing. (Reviewer-2 obligation; the reviewer's claim that this check is agent-invoked is not established by the supplied source.)
scope_limits: No caller of task_service.complete() (agent tool, lifecycle hook, or API route) appears in the supplied views; the agent-mediation framing exists only as module-docstring narrative, so no agent_entry_binding evidence is cited.
partially_complete() and fail() intentionally bypass the completion checks and are outside this contract.
The transition() state machine (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS) is a secondary layer; only its role in gating COMPLETED is in scope.

contracts.declared_mechanism: permissions.require_connection looks up the connection filtered by user_id and provider, fails closed with PermissionDenied and audit_service.record DENIED entries (connection.access_denied / connection.write_denied) on non-ownership/missing connection, non-CONNECTED status, or write not enabled, and only then returns the connection to the caller; each guarded tool calls it as its first statement before any provider SDK use.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Accessing a ServiceConnection where no matching (user_id, provider) connection exists or conn.owner_agent_id differs from the calling agent_id; accessing a connection whose status is not CONNECTED; or requesting need_write on a connection whose write_enabled flag is false.
pending_binding_information: Whether HTTP routes or other callers invoke these impl functions directly outside function_tool dispatch; the guard would still apply, but tool-dispatch binding is only evidenced for the registered tools.
contracts.protected_operation: Tool-mediated use of external provider connections in the supplied views: Gmail reads (list_recent_emails_impl), Gmail draft-approval creation (draft_external_email_impl), Gmail sends (send_approved_email_impl), calendar reads (get_agenda_impl), calendar change requests (request_calendar_change_impl), and calendar applies (apply_calendar_change_impl).
contracts.protected_resource: ServiceConnection records scoped by (user_id, provider) and the external provider APIs (Gmail, Google Calendar) whose access they authorize.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every tool execution that touches an external provider connection must first pass permissions.require_connection: an agent may not access a ServiceConnection it does not own, use a connection that is not CONNECTED, or perform write access when write_enabled is false; denial is fail-closed (PermissionDenied plus an audit record) and cannot be altered by model output or routing decisions.
scope_limits: The supplied views demonstrate the guard on six tools across email_agent.py and calendar_agent.py; the module docstring claim that every connection-touching tool calls require_connection cannot be verified repository-wide.
Write-path enforcement for the gmail send and calendar apply is co-declared in those two contracts; this contract states the standalone connection-access authorization obligation, including reads.
Audit-record emission on denial is part of the mechanism; audit delivery reliability is not verifiable from the supplied views.
